rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh either failed to recognize their messenger or are denying him deliberately; deliberate denial is a strategy that will backfire.
rows.anchor: or are they denying him intentionally. In the latter case, this ploy will work badly for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the messenger insane exposes the accusers' own insanity; he is not mad, but brings absolute truth that will come to pass.
rows.anchor: then this is a proof of their own lunacy. The messenger is in no such state.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their accusation mirrors a patient who dislikes bitter medicine and dismisses the doctor's advice instead of recognizing his own illness.
rows.anchor: When a patient regards the medicines of his doctor to be sour and is not prepared to take them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human desires and truth are radically opposed, with incompatible demands and requirements.
rows.anchor: Both are as far apart from one another as the East and the West. The demands and requisites of both are very different.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If truth were reshaped to their demands, the moral order would collapse because they champion evil, injustice, vice, dishonesty, polytheism, and denial of Judgment.
rows.anchor: advocates of evil instead of good, injustice instead of justice, vice instead of virtue, dishonesty instead of honesty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Admitting polytheism would make the cosmos unsustainable: each deity would take its creation and attack another, as verse 91 explains.
rows.anchor: if such was the case, each deity would have taken his creation and walked away, and would have attacked another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People want truth to accommodate them, but salvation requires following truth; life requires it regardless of whether it tastes sour or sweet.
rows.anchor: If they want life, then they must follow the truth whether it is sour or sweet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wording repeats the warning of verse 69: the Qur'an is their divinely given reminder and conclusive communication, not a storyteller's tale.
rows.anchor: sound the same warning that is sounded earlier in verse 69 in different words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is God's reminder sent to establish the truth conclusively; if they ignore it, earlier nations' fate awaits them.
rows.anchor: This is their share of reminder that God has sent them for conclusive communication of the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent messengers to every nation to remind it of the Hereafter; nations that honored the reminder succeeded, while those that did not were destroyed.
rows.anchor: Nations which duly valued this reminder succeeded and those which did not were destroyed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet gives freely what he received freely and asks no fee; opponents who disregard the favor deprive themselves, and rejection cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: he is distributing free what he gained free and not asking them for any charges.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward is superior, and He provides for His messengers' truth-preaching; righteous people who continue their work likewise receive its provisions.
rows.anchor: God’s messengers are advocates of the truth; their preaching has all its provisions.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet calls them to the straight path, which reaches their true destination, but following it requires belief in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: The straight path towards which the Prophet (sws) is calling people leads them to their actual destination

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those expecting a day of reward can sacrifice immediate pleasures; without that expectation, people keep following desire away from the path.
rows.anchor: Only those people can sacrifice the near at hand pleasures of this life who are waiting for a day of reward.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The salvation path is clear and straight; evasion stems from hearts lacking belief in the Hereafter, which inevitably leads people astray.
rows.anchor: those who do not believe in the Hereafter have gone astray from the straight path.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the Hereafter, worldly existence seems incoherent and impossible to navigate rightly; Islahi says this point recurs elsewhere in his exegesis.
rows.anchor: those who do not believe in the Hereafter have gone astray from the straight path.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is elliptical: had God tested them to admonish them, then shown mercy by removing hardship, they would have returned to rebellious wandering.
rows.anchor: A part of the conditional clause stated in this verse is suppressed in accordance with linguistic principles.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment signs would not reform them; any submission during trial would be temporary, and leaders would later explain hardship away as unrelated to belief or character.
rows.anchor: the signs of punishment which they demand are of no avail. If ever they show submission, it is temporary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because such people do not benefit from signs, the Prophet should disregard their demand for a punishment sign.
rows.anchor: if these people demand a sign of punishment, he should ignore them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The history of earlier people who behaved similarly shows that warnings never reform them, so the Prophet should not expect Quraysh to change.
rows.anchor: the past bears witness that people of this nature never learn a lesson from warnings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun 'them' refers to people of earlier nations, not Quraysh; Arabic commonly uses such a pronoun here.
rows.anchor: it is the people of the previous nations who behaved similarly. It is common in Arabic for such pronouns to occur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the wording eloquent because seizing one group is like seizing another when both committed the same offense.
rows.anchor: seizing one is like seizing the other because both are guilty of the same crime.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first form describes inward humility, while the second names the outward wailing and crying that results from it.
rows.anchor: The former signifies the humility of the heart and the latter refers to the wailing and crying

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says an incomplete verb is suppressed before the verb of pleading in 23:76.
rows.anchor: an incomplete verb is suppressed before

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings will not reform them until God sends decisive severe punishment on a nation persisting in denial after conclusive communication; little respite follows, and its hopes collapse.
rows.anchor: these rebukes and warnings will not make them mend their ways until the time arrives when God will send down His harsh torment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ears, eyes, and hearts are given for hearing wisdom, seeing God's inward and outward signs, and reflecting on their consequences; that is their proper use.
rows.anchor: their ears hear the words of counsel and wisdom being narrated to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seek punishment instead of rational proofs; people who act only when driven by a whip differ little from animals.
rows.anchor: people only spring into action when forced by a whip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being seldom grateful conveys longing and sorrow.
rows.anchor: The words “yet, very seldom are you grateful” express yearning and sorrow.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True gratitude starts by acknowledging gifts, benefiting from them properly, and thanking their provider.
rows.anchor: acknowledgement of favours means that a person tries to truly benefit from it and be grateful to the provider of these favours.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a farmer sows for harvest, the One who scattered humanity across earth will gather people to Himself.
rows.anchor: When a farmer sows seeds in his field, the purpose is to harvest the crop that will emerge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering belongs to God alone, like a harvest only its owner may claim; the verse compresses an argument for Judgment and monotheism.
rows.anchor: people should remember that they will only be gathered at His place. How can someone else share his harvested crop?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase denotes day and night following each other with remarkable punctuality.
rows.anchor: coming of the day and night one after the other with amazing punctuality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an points to the alternation of night and day at many places and presents further lessons from it, which Islahi discusses in his exegesis.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ān has directed attention to this sign at many instances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their precise succession shows the universe is subject to God's laws; neither night nor day has independent authority, and only God controls them.
rows.anchor: This coming of the day and night with such precision in timing shows that this universe is subjected to the laws of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their radically different natures coexist in harmony, evidence that one powerful, wise will orders conflicting elements for the whole universe's good.
rows.anchor: there exists complete harmony between the night and day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daily awakening after sleep reminds each person that God can awaken humanity from its Barzakh sleep whenever He wills.
rows.anchor: Getting up in the morning after a comfortable night’s sleep is a reminder of the hereafter for every person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the preceding clear signs, the deniers repeat their predecessors' objection, calling resurrection after death and decay ancient tales.
rows.anchor: they regard all this as fables of the past that mean nothing and say precisely what their predecessors had said.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi introduces the next question as exposing a contradiction in the disbelievers' views; this excerpt ends before he states the contrast.
rows.anchor: This verse points to the contradictory views of these disbelievers: on the one hand,
